messages:
jordan: Quick Q from the all-hands Q&A threadmdashhow do trial credits and prorated charges interact when a customer switches from trial -> paid mid-cycle? Customers ask if they lose their trial credits or if billing is pro-rated.

matt: Short answer: trial credits are consumed first regardless of plan. If they upgrade mid-cycle, they still use leftover trial credits until expiry or depletion. Any monetary charge beyond credits is prorated based on the paid plan start time.

sophia: To add: we treat trial credits like a separate credit bucket with TTL. Example: acct has 1000 trial tokens (expire 2026-06-01) + switches to Starter on 2026-05-10 with monthly fee. Usage flow: 1) consume trial bucket, 2) consume monthly plan allocation, 3) charge overage or top-up.

jordan: If we bill a prorated month up front, do we invoice immediately or at next invoice run?
sam: We generate an immediate interim invoice for any prorated subscription fee at upgrade time. Usage charges still show on the normal billing cycle but with a breakdown referencing the interim invoice.

riley: Metering delay note: tokens are reported to billing within ~30s for hosted API. For Dedicated we have a short aggregation window (90s) so live dashboards may lag. This affects near-real-time credits visibility during a plan change.

jordan: Curious about refunds: if a customer downgrades and has unused committed capacity, is there an automated proration refund?
sam: Not automated. Unused committed capacity refunds require a finance review. Small cases (<$500) can be handled by support credits; larger ones need contract review. We aim for a 5-business-day turnaround.

andre: Customer experience point: document this in the Console tooltip and add a quick "what happens on upgrade/downgrade" explainer. Customers get confused about TTL vs plan quotas.
sophia: Good call. We'll add a short modal explaining: "Trial credits are separate. Upgrades change quotas but not existing credit TTLs."

jordan: Any gotchas for multi-region customers or cross-account consolidated billing?
riley: For consolidated billing, credits are applied at the invoice-level priority rules (promo -> trial -> plan allocations). For multi-region Dedicated, provisioning latency can cause short periods where rate limits don't reflect the new plan; we surface warnings in Console when that happens.

jordan: Can we show an example invoice entry so sales can explain to customers?
sam: Example line items: 
```
2026-05-10 - Starter plan prorated (20/30 days) - $66.67
2026-05-10 - Interim invoice balance applied: -$50 (trial credits)
2026-05-31 - Usage overage (tokens) - $12.34
```

andre: I'll draft a short FAQ blurb and pass to docs. Also recommend a tooltip linking to the example invoice.
billing-bot: Created ticket BILL-598: Add Console explainer copy, example invoice lines, and guidance for support on small refunds; assign to @sam.

jordan: Thanks all. I'll add this snippet to the all-hands notes and route to sales enablement.

matt: Thanks 44d. If any customer cases are urgent, ping me and finance directly. End thread.
